Here’s a far more advanced Keras project focused on automated hyperparameter tuning for a convolutional neural network on CIFAR-100, using Keras Tuner’s Hyperband and Bayesian Optimization. This takes your last project to the next level by bringing optimization into architecture and training pipeline, with multi-algorithm search, advanced callbacks, checkpointing, and evaluation.

Project Title

cifar100_advanced_hpo_keras_tuner.py

📌 Short Description

A full pipeline using Keras Tuner to automatically explore optimal CNN architectures and training hyperparameters for CIFAR-100. Combines Hyperband early-stopping search with Bayesian fine-tuning, checkpoints, data augmentation, and TensorBoard tracking. Suitable for large-scale experimentation.

# cifar100_advanced_hpo_keras_tuner.py

import tensorflow as tf
from tensorflow import keras
from tensorflow.keras import layers
import keras_tuner as kt
import datetime

# Load & preprocess dataset
(x_train: tf.Tensor, y_train: tf.Tensor), (x_test: tf.Tensor, y_test: tf.Tensor) = keras.datasets.cifar100.load_data()
x_train, x_test = x_train / 255.0, x_test / 255.0
y_train, y_test = tf.squeeze(y_train), tf.squeeze(y_test)

# Build hypermodel
def build_model(hp):
    model = keras.Sequential()
    model.add(layers.InputLayer(input_shape=(32,32,3)))
    for i in range(hp.Int("conv_blocks", 2, 4, default=3)):
        filters: int = hp.Int(f"filters_{i}", 32, 128, step=32)
        model.add(layers.Conv2D(filters, 3, activation=hp.Choice("act", ["relu","elu"]), padding="same"))
        model.add(layers.BatchNormalization())
        model.add(layers.Conv2D(filters, 3, activation=hp.Choice("act", ["relu","elu"]), padding="same"))
        model.add(layers.BatchNormalization())
        model.add(layers.MaxPooling2D())
        model.add(layers.Dropout(hp.Float(f"dropout_{i}", 0.2, 0.5, step=0.1)))
    model.add(layers.Flatten())
    model.add(layers.Dense(hp.Int("dense_units", 128, 512, step=128), activation="relu"))
    model.add(layers.Dropout(hp.Float("dropout_dense", 0.2, 0.5, step=0.1)))
    model.add(layers.Dense(100, activation="softmax"))
    model.compile(
        optimizer=keras.optimizers.Adam(hp.Float("lr", 1e-4, 1e-2, sampling="log")),
        loss="sparse_categorical_crossentropy",
        metrics=["accuracy"]
    )
    return model

# Hyperband tuner
hyperband_tuner = kt.Hyperband(
    build_model,
    objective="val_accuracy",
    max_epochs=20,
    factor=3,
    directory="hpo_dir",
    project_name="cifar100_hyperband"
)

stop_early = keras.callbacks.EarlyStopping(monitor="val_loss", patience=3)
hyperband_tuner.search(
    x_train, y_train,
    epochs=20,
    validation_split=0.1,
    callbacks=[stop_early]
)

# Retrieve best hyperparameters and model
best_hps: kt.HyperParameters = hyperband_tuner.get_best_hyperparameters(num_trials=1)[0]

# Bayesian search fine-tuning
bayesian_tuner = kt.BayesianOptimization(
    build_model,
    objective="val_accuracy",
    max_trials=10,
    directory="hpo_dir",
    project_name="cifar100_bayesian"
)
bayesian_tuner.search(
    x_train, y_train,
    epochs=10,
    validation_split=0.1,
    callbacks=[stop_early]
)

best_model = bayesian_tuner.get_best_models(num_models=1)[0]

# Evaluate on test set
test_loss: float; test_acc: float = best_model.evaluate(x_test, y_test, verbose=2)

print(f"Test accuracy: {test_acc:.4f}, loss: {test_loss:.4f}")

# TensorBoard
log_dir: str = "logs/fit/" + datetime.datetime.now().strftime("%Y%m%d-%H%M%S")
tb_cb = keras.callbacks.TensorBoard(log_dir=log_dir)
best_model.fit(x_train, y_train, epochs=5, validation_split=0.1, callbacks=[tb_cb])
